snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Unit 8 Hook: Puli Thevar: First. Kattabomman: Kayathar. Marudu: Lion. 1801: Proclamation. 1806: Vellore Mutiny. Velu Nachiyar: Heroine.

quick_notes.title: Puli Thevar (Nerkattumseval)
quick_notes.detail: The first Indian to resist British rule (1755). Defeated Alexander Heron. Later defeated by Yusuf Khan (Khan Sahib).
quick_notes.explanation: Puli Thevar was a local chieftain from Nerkattumseval, a town in present-day Tamil Nadu, and he is considered the first Indian ruler to fight against British rule, meaning the control of the British East India Company, in the year 1755. He won a battle against Alexander Heron, a British officer who was leading Company forces. However, Puli Thevar was later defeated by Yusuf Khan, also known as Khan Sahib, who was a commander working for the British East India Company. This defeat ended Puli Thevar

quick_notes.title: Veerapandiya Kattabomman
quick_notes.detail: Palayakkarar of Panchalankurichi. Confrontation with Jackson (Collector). Captured and hanged at Kayathar (Oct 16, 1799).
quick_notes.explanation: Veerapandiya Kattabomman was a Palayakkarar, which means a local chieftain or ruler of a small territory, of the place called Panchalankurichi in present-day Tamil Nadu. He came into conflict with the British East India Company's Collector, an official in charge of revenue collection and administration, named Jackson. Kattabomman refused to pay taxes and challenged British authority, leading to a confrontation. He was eventually captured by the British and was hanged to death at Kayathar on October 16, 1799.

quick_notes.title: Marudu Brothers (Sivagangai)
quick_notes.detail: Periya Marudu and Chinna Marudu. Issued the "Tiruchirappalli Proclamation" (1801). Known as "Lion of Sivagangai". Hanged at Tiruppathur.
quick_notes.explanation: The Marudu Brothers, whose names were Periya Marudu and Chinna Marudu, were two brothers who ruled the Sivagangai region in present-day Tamil Nadu. In the year 1801, they issued a document called the "Tiruchirappalli Proclamation", which was a public announcement declaring their intention to fight against the British East India Company's control over their land. Because of their brave resistance, they were given the title "Lion of Sivagangai". The British eventually captured the brothers, and they were executed by being hanged at a place called Tiruppathur.

quick_notes.title: Velu Nachiyar
quick_notes.detail: First woman to fight the British. Reclaimed Sivagangai with help of Hyder Ali and Marudu brothers. Used "Kuyili" (suicide bomber).
quick_notes.explanation: Velu Nachiyar was a queen from the 18th century who is recognized as the first Indian ruler to fight against the British East India Company. She ruled the kingdom of Sivagangai, which is in present-day Tamil Nadu, and after losing her kingdom to the British she fought back and successfully reclaimed it. To achieve this, she formed an alliance with Hyder Ali, the ruler of Mysore, and the Marudu brothers, who were commanders from the nearby kingdom of Sivagangai. She also used a method called a "Kuyili," which refers to a suicide bomber – a person who deliberately blows themselves up to destroy enemy weapons or soldiers. This tactic was famously carried out by a woman named Kuyili who sacrificed herself by setting fire to a British ammunition store. Velu Nachiyar's actions make her a pioneering figure in the Indian resistance against colonial rule.

quick_notes.title: Vellore Mutiny (July 10, 1806)
quick_notes.detail: First major revolt in South India. Cause : New military regulations/turban. Suppressed by Rollo Gillespie.
quick_notes.explanation: The Vellore Mutiny was the first major revolt by Indian soldiers against the British East India Company in South India. It happened on July 10, 1806, in the town of Vellore, which is in present-day Tamil Nadu. The main cause was a new military regulation that forced Indian soldiers to shave their beards and remove their caste marks, and also required them to wear a new type of turban that looked like a European hat, which offended their religious and cultural beliefs. The mutiny was quickly suppressed by British forces led by General Rollo Gillespie, who stormed the fort and killed hundreds of rebel soldiers. This event is important because it showed early signs of Indian resistance against British rule, nearly 50 years before the larger Revolt of 1857.

Or what happened at the 'Vellore Mutiny'? Let's master the rebellion today.
